rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 5-6 report the authors' own design, lab calibration tests (Tables 2-5) and a one-week field trial of an ESP32 drip system with a SEN0308 capacitive soil moisture sensor growing spring onions in a single acrylic container.
rows.notes: The study does use the SEN0308 sensor but reports no water-saving result. It only computes that each onion received 0.676 gallons/week (Equations 1-2) and compares this with a recommended 0.623 gallons/week from a gardening website, concluding the system supplies adequate moisture. There is no baseline or non-sensor comparison, no 11% saving figure, no yield measurement. Single container, one week, potting soil in Qatar. The 11% water saving / 12.05% yield figures in the passage do not come from this study.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 5-6 report the authors' own system build, sensor calibration tests and a one-week field trial growing spring onions from bulbs under the sensor-controlled drip system (Figure 18, Figure 20).
rows.notes: The study reports only a qualitative observation that after one week spring onions had begun to grow atop a few bulbs and looked healthy (Section 6, Figure 18). No yield was measured, no comparison with a control or conventional irrigation, and no 12.05% yield increase is reported. Single container, one week, one crop. The yield figure in the passage must come from the other cited source.

notes: Full text appears complete. The paper is a system-engineering demonstration (ESP32 + SEN0308 + DS18B20 + DHT22 + flow sensor + solenoid) tested in one acrylic container over one week; it contains sensor calibration data and a weekly water-application calculation but no water-saving or yield comparisons against any baseline.
